name: Mintokling Guest House
summary: A long-running, family-run guest house on Bhanu Path, a short walk below MG Marg. Rooms are simple and warm, the garden is quiet, and the welcome is Sikkimese rather than corporate.
body: Mintokling has hosted travellers in Gangtok for decades and is run by a local Bhutia family. The house sits in a garden off Bhanu Path, close enough to walk to MG Marg in ten minutes but far enough to sleep without traffic noise. Rooms are wood-panelled, clean and plainly furnished, with hot water and heaters in winter.

We book it for travellers who want a calm base with a personal touch at a fair price. Breakfast is home-style, the hosts give honest advice on permits and road conditions, and the dining room is a good place to meet other guests before a Tsomgo or Zuluk trip.
why: Walking distance from MG Marg without the noise
Family hosts who know the permit system well
Fair prices for a quiet, clean room
Garden and sitting areas that feel like a home

faqs.q: How far is Mintokling Guest House from MG Marg?
faqs.a: It is about a ten-minute walk downhill from MG Marg along Bhanu Path, and a little longer coming back up because Gangtok is steep. Local taxis can drop you at the gate if you have heavy bags. The location keeps you close to cafés and shops while giving you a quieter night.

faqs.q: Is Mintokling suitable for families with children?
faqs.a: Yes, for families who are happy with a simple, homely guest house. Some rooms take an extra bed, and the garden gives children space to move. There is no lift or pool, and the approach involves steps, so families with prams or elderly members with limited mobility should ask about ground-floor rooms when booking.

faqs.q: Can the guest house help arrange Tsomgo and Nathu La permits?
faqs.a: Permits for Tsomgo and Nathu La are issued through registered travel agents, and the hosts can put you in touch with reliable ones. You will need photo ID and passport-size photos, and Nathu La permits must be applied for a day ahead. Rules are indicative. Check current status before you travel.

name: Hotel Sonam Delek
summary: An established mid-range hotel on Tibet Road, a few minutes' walk from MG Marg, with rooms that look out over the valley towards Kangchenjunga on clear mornings. It is reliable, central and good value for the location.
body: Sonam Delek is one of Gangtok's older family-run hotels and sits on Tibet Road, just above the main market area. Valley-facing rooms on the upper floors catch the Kangchenjunga range at sunrise from October to April when the sky is clear. The restaurant serves Sikkimese, Tibetan and Indian food.

We use it for Value-tier trips because it is central, well kept and run by people who understand what travellers on a tight schedule need: early breakfasts on Tsomgo days, help with taxis, and somewhere warm to come back to. Ask for a mountain-view room and book early for October and May.
why: Central on Tibet Road, a short walk to MG Marg
Mountain-view rooms on clear days
Early breakfasts for permit-day departures
Consistent service at a fair mid-range price

faqs.q: Do rooms at Hotel Sonam Delek have mountain views?
faqs.a: The valley-facing rooms on the upper floors look towards the Kangchenjunga range, which shows best on clear mornings between October and April. In the monsoon, cloud usually hides the peaks. Mountain-view rooms cost a little more and sell out first in peak season, so ask for one specifically when you book.

faqs.q: Is there parking near Hotel Sonam Delek?
faqs.a: Tibet Road is narrow and parking is limited, as it is across central Gangtok. Most guests arrive by taxi and do not need parking. If you are driving your own car, ask the hotel in advance where to leave it, and expect a short walk from the nearest space.

faqs.q: What food does the hotel restaurant serve?
faqs.a: The restaurant serves a mix of Sikkimese, Tibetan, Indian and simple continental dishes, including momos, thukpa and dal-rice meals. Vegetarian options are always available. Many guests eat dinner in town on MG Marg and use the hotel for breakfast, which is served early on request for Tsomgo and Nathu La days.

name: The Elgin Nor-Khill
summary: A heritage hotel built in the 1930s as the royal guest house of the Chogyals of Sikkim, now run by Elgin Hotels. It has period rooms, a large garden and a quiet location near Paljor Stadium.
body: Nor-Khill was built by the royal family of Sikkim to house state guests, and the building keeps its old character: wooden floors, Sikkimese painted details, photographs from the kingdom years and a lawn that catches the afternoon sun. It sits below the town centre near Paljor Stadium, a short taxi ride or a steep walk from MG Marg.

We book it for Comfort-tier travellers who want history and calm rather than a modern tower. Rates usually include breakfast and often dinner, the staff are experienced, and the hotel handles Tsomgo and Nathu La arrangements smoothly. Rooms vary in size and view, so it is worth paying for a garden or valley-facing room.
why: A former royal guest house with real Sikkimese history
Quiet garden setting away from traffic
Experienced staff who arrange permit days well
Meal plans that keep the daily budget predictable

faqs.q: What is the history of the Nor-Khill hotel?
faqs.a: Nor-Khill was built in the early 1930s by the ruling Namgyal family of Sikkim as a guest house for official visitors to the kingdom. It became a hotel after Sikkim joined India in 1975 and is now part of the Elgin group, which also runs heritage hotels in Darjeeling and Kalimpong.

faqs.q: Is the Elgin Nor-Khill within walking distance of MG Marg?
faqs.a: It is about 1 km from MG Marg, but the walk is steep uphill on the way back, so most guests take a local taxi for ₹100–200. The location is quieter than the hotels on MG Marg itself, which suits travellers who want to rest well between long mountain days.

faqs.q: Does the hotel include meals in the room rate?
faqs.a: Most rate plans include breakfast, and many packages include dinner as well. Meal plans change by season and booking channel, so check what is included when you reserve. Having dinner at the hotel is convenient after a long Tsomgo or Nathu La day, when you may not want to go out again.

name: Mayfair Spa Resort and Casino
summary: A large, full-service resort on the outskirts of Gangtok with a spa, indoor pool and landscaped grounds. It is the most resort-like stay in the region and suits travellers who want space and facilities.
body: Mayfair is built in a Sikkimese-inspired style on a forested hillside a short drive below the town centre. Rooms are large and well heated, and the property has an indoor heated pool, a spa, several restaurants and a casino. It is popular for honeymoons, family celebrations and travellers who want to stay put between excursions.

We offer it in the Comfort tier for travellers who value facilities over being able to walk to MG Marg. The trade-off is distance: you will need a taxi into town each evening. For a first visit to Sikkim, many guests split their nights between Mayfair and a central hotel.
why: Indoor heated pool and spa after cold lake days
Large, warm rooms with good beds
Calm grounds away from town traffic
Good for honeymoons and family celebrations

faqs.q: How far is Mayfair Gangtok from MG Marg?
faqs.a: The resort is a short drive below the town centre, usually 15–25 minutes to MG Marg depending on traffic. You cannot comfortably walk to town, so budget for a taxi each time, around ₹300–500 each way. The resort can arrange cars for sightseeing, Rumtek and permit trips.

faqs.q: Is Mayfair Gangtok good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: It is one of the most popular honeymoon choices in Sikkim because of its spa, heated indoor pool, large rooms and quiet grounds. Many couples combine two nights here with a more central hotel. Book early for May, October and the Christmas to New Year period, when rates rise sharply.

faqs.q: Do I need to stay at the casino resort to visit the casino?
faqs.a: No, but the casino has its own entry rules and age limits, and it is a small part of what the resort offers. Most guests come for the rooms, spa and setting. Casino rules, entry fees and timings are set by the operator and can change, so ask at the desk.

name: Zuluk village homestays
price_band: ₹1,200–2,000 per person per night with meals
summary: Zuluk has no hotels in the usual sense, only family homestays in the small village and army settlement. Rooms are basic but warm, and the price usually includes dinner and breakfast.
body: Homestays in Zuluk are simple wooden or concrete houses with two to six guest rooms, thick blankets, and shared or attached bathrooms with hot water by bucket or geyser. Meals are home-cooked: dal, rice, vegetables, eggs, and sometimes local pork or chicken. Electricity can be patchy and mobile signal is limited to some networks.

Most homestay owners also arrange the Zuluk Protected Area Permit through Rongli, which makes them the easiest way to book the Silk Route. We choose hosts we have stayed with, who keep rooms clean and give honest advice about road conditions in snow. Expect cold nights at about 3,000 m and pack warm layers.
why: The only real way to stay overnight in Zuluk
Hosts usually arrange the Rongli permit for you
Home-cooked meals included in the price
Early access to Thambi viewpoint for sunrise

faqs.a: Rooms are not centrally heated. Most hosts give thick quilts and some provide electric heaters, which work only when the power supply is steady. Nights drop below freezing from November to March. Bring thermal layers, a warm hat and socks, and ask your host about heaters and hot water when you book.

faqs.q: Do Zuluk homestays arrange the Silk Route permit?
faqs.a: Most do. You send scans of photo ID and passport photos a few days ahead, and the host or their agent collects the Protected Area Permit at Rongli, where it is checked on the way up. Only Indian nationals are allowed. Rules are indicative. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What food is served in Zuluk homestays?
faqs.a: Expect simple home cooking: rice, dal, a vegetable dish, pickles, eggs, and chicken or pork on request. Breakfast is usually bread, eggs or puri-sabzi, with tea. Vegetarians are easily catered for. Tell your host about dietary needs in advance, because supplies come up from Rongli and shopping is limited.

name: Aritar village homestays
price_band: ₹1,200–2,200 per person per night with meals
summary: Aritar has a good spread of family homestays around Lampokhari lake and the surrounding villages. They are clean, friendly and cheap, and most include dinner and breakfast.
body: Aritar's homestays range from rooms in farmhouses among cardamom and vegetable plots to newer purpose-built cottages near the lake. Hosts are mostly Nepali-speaking farming families, and meals use their own produce: rice, local greens, squash, dal, and sometimes gundruk or sel roti.

We use Aritar homestays as the first or last night on a Silk Route trip because the village sits at a comfortable 1,400 m, which helps before the climb to Zuluk. Rooms near the lake are convenient for an evening walk; those higher up give better morning views. Most hosts can also help with the Zuluk permit.
why: A gentle first night before the climb to Zuluk
Home-grown food and friendly farming families
Walk to Lampokhari lake and Mankhim
Hosts can help organise the Silk Route permit

faqs.q: Is Aritar a good first stop on the Silk Route?
faqs.a: Yes. At about 1,400 m, Aritar gives your body a gentle night before Zuluk at about 3,000 m and the high road above it. It is roughly 105 km from Siliguri, so you arrive in good time. Next morning the drive to Zuluk via Rongli takes about 2.5–3 hours.

faqs.q: Do Aritar homestays have attached bathrooms?
faqs.a: Most newer homestays have attached bathrooms with geysers, while older farmhouse rooms sometimes share one. Power cuts happen in the monsoon. If an attached bathroom matters to you, ask the host directly when booking, and request a photo of the room if you are unsure.

faqs.q: Can I walk around Aritar from my homestay?
faqs.a: Yes. Lampokhari lake has a level path around it, and the walk up to Mankhim viewpoint takes about 30–45 minutes from the lake. Village lanes lead through cardamom and vegetable plots. Paths are steep in places and slippery in rain, so wear shoes with good grip.
